findings.title: Potential NullPointerException in getCredentials when user is not in storage
findings.body: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(RealmModel, UserModel)`, `myUser` is retrieved via `getMyUser(user)` and immediately dereferenced on lines 235 (`myUser.recoveryCodes != null`) and 247 (`myUser.otp != null`) without a null check. In contrast, `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isConfiguredFor`, and `isValid` in the same class all guard against `myUser == null` before accessing fields on `myUser`. If `getCredentials` is invoked for a user not present in the `users` map, it will throw a `NullPointerException` instead of returning an empty stream.

findings.title: hasRecoveryCodes does not normalize username to lowercase before map lookup
findings.body: `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` stores and looks up users in the shared `users` (`userPasswords`) map using `translateUserName(username)` (i.e. `username.toLowerCase()`). In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageFactory.hasRecoveryCodes(String username)`, `userPasswords.get(username)` is called directly without lowercasing `username`, so calling `hasRecoveryCodes` with any uppercase characters will return `false` even when the user has recovery codes stored.
